I merged all investigator findings, giving strongest weight to files implicated by multiple confident reports and direct stack evidence. All reports agree that src/vs/workbench/services/textfile/common/textFileEditorModel.ts and src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts are the most likely locations for listener leaks, as these files directly manage event listeners for text editor models. However, precedent issues do not match this component well, so confidence is not high.

Multiple highly confident reports point to the Win32 update service (updateService.win32.ts) and related Electron main process files as the locus of the bug, which involves a file-lock preventing an update due to a process holding a handle on 'old_Code - Insiders.exe'. Recommendations merge evidence from issues #294546 and #324944 (both >0.85 confidence), weighing heavily on updateService.win32.ts where update/rename is controlled, with secondary focus on main Electron process files that may handle process and mutex logic, and the Inno Setup script that packages update logic. Overlapping file suggestions are merged and sorted by frequency and report confidence.

The bug is caused by a split in how the disabled state for built-in skills is persisted and read: the Disable action writes to one storage key, while the Agents window reads from another (or not at all), with the result that disabled items are neither shown as disabled nor dropped from the agent bundle. A robust fix must coordinate both the data writes (aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts) and the reading/selection logic (agentCustomizationItemsModel.ts, agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts), merging built-in skills directly from the prompts service in the UI model so they remain visible and toggleable while disabled. These three files are cited explicitly and implicated by the investigation. Other files mentioned in past issues either handle unrelated domains or focus on skill discovery logic rather than state syncing, so they are not included here. Thus, the most likely files to be changed are those directly managing customization disable/enable actions, state storage, and the item provider/model for skills display and syncing.

Multiple strong precedents agree the bug's root is in how agentHostAuth.ts and agentHostAuthenticationService.ts forward and interpret empty tokens when a new Agent Host client starts, accidentally revoking global credentials on transient cache misses. Confidence is high that fixes must coordinate agentHostAuth.ts (token cache/init logic) and agentHostAuthenticationService.ts (server-side token application and revocation), with supporting changes to authentication.ts and extHostAuthentication.ts if necessary to prevent false revocation. Test updates in agentHostAuth.test.ts are likely needed to guard against regression.
